audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 said Skill where the packet gives Olaf and the prose says Olaf wins first contact; first item said Olaf where whys[5] literally calls it a stalemate; 2+ items said Olaf where the packet and whys[6] both say Tahm Kench.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page called the grey-health mechanic 'W-devour mitigation' and 'W-mitigation' in seven places, and said Ragnarok 'cleanses' the Tongue Lash stun.
audit.why: Grey health is Thick Skin (E, 3s) — it stores a percentage of damage taken and either converts it to a shield on cast or heals it back out of combat. W is Abyssal Dive, a 21s dive that knocks up; R is Devour. The page merged all three into one imaginary ability, so a reader tracking 'his W' was tracking nothing real. The other correction that changes play: Abyssal Dive's knockup carries the displacement flag whose own note reads 'ignored by unstoppable', so Ragnarok does NOT stop it — the level-6 dive is not the clean window the page promised.
audit.corrected: Separated Thick Skin, Abyssal Dive and Devour throughout; stated the three-stack An Acquired Taste condition on Tongue Lash's stun; narrowed Ragnarok to the stun and stated the knockup it cannot stop.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] ('E for true damage') and dosFull[2] ('R to cleanse his stun') both carried unrelated bodies, and dosFull[0] described Abyssal Dive as an 'escape + shield'.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive has no shield on it, and neither do-entry told the reader how to do the thing it named.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten; Abyssal Dive redescribed as the dive and knockup it is, with its 21s cooldown.

edits.before: Tahm Kench is one of the few melees you can't simply out-trade on stats, because his passive turns your E true damage and Q-auto chunks into grey health he heals back the moment he steps away. Win the early levels anyway: hit your level 2-3 Q-slow into E before his grey-health pool is deep, and force the trade while his W-devour is on cooldown. Don't sit in Q tongue range when you have no follow-up — eating that stun for nothing lets him reset the trade or just farm you off the wave.
edits.after: Tahm Kench is one of the few melees you can't simply out-trade on stats, because Thick Skin stores a share of everything you land and either converts it to a shield or heals it back once he steps away. Win the early levels anyway: hit your level 2-3 Q-slow into E before that bar is deep, and force the trade while Abyssal Dive is on its 21s cooldown. Don't sit at Tongue Lash range with no follow-up — a third stack of An Acquired Taste turns it into a stun, and eating that for nothing lets him reset the trade.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 even out because he stops dying to single combos once grey health and W-mitigation come online — every E you land partly feeds a bar he reclaims. Keep stacking short trades with axe-reset slows and W omnivamp so you stay ahead on the wave and bank a CS/plates lead. At 6 your Ragnarok is the key tool: it cleanses his Q tongue stun, so if you have a gold edge you can dive through the one thing that peels you, but don't all-in even when he can grey-health your burst and W you out.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 even out because he stops dying to single combos once Thick Skin is online — every E you land partly feeds a bar he reclaims. Keep stacking short trades with axe resets and Tough It Out's shield so you stay ahead on the wave and bank a CS and plates lead. At 6 Ragnarok matters but is not a blank cheque: it blocks his Tongue Lash stun while you keep attacking, and Abyssal Dive's knockup is a displacement it does not stop, so dive only when you already hold a gold lead.

edits.before: This is where he takes over. A two-item Tahm Kench grey-heals your flat E true damage faster than you can re-apply it, his W mitigates your biggest hit, and his percent-HP simply out-lasts a short-fight kit like yours. Worse, his R lets him roam and snowball a second lane off your stalemate while your own splitpush stalls into a tank that won't die. Convert every early-to-mid plate, kill, and herald into objectives before two items land — if it goes even to late, he wins the map.
edits.after: This is where he takes over. A two-item Tahm Kench heals your flat E true damage back faster than you can re-apply it, Thick Skin turns your biggest hit into a shield, and a passive that scales off his total health out-lasts a short-fight kit like yours. Worse, Devour lets him roam and snowball a second lane off your stalemate while your own splitpush stalls into a tank that won't die. Convert every early-to-mid plate, kill and herald into objectives before two items land — if it goes late, he wins the map.
